entries.title: 开始前先确认

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 1.1 找到你需要的功能
entries.text: 你要做什么 到哪里操作 修改设备 root/admin 密码 账号安全，见第 2 章 让设备用密钥连接服务器 密钥管理、已部署主机，见第 3 章 复制密钥、处理服务器身份变化 密钥管理、已知主机指纹，见第 4 章 配置设备证书和双向证书认证 HTTPS 证书，见第 5 章 交换加密配置包 Config Pack，见第 6 章；通用应用功能尚未完成

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 1.2 账号与设备身份不是一回事
entries.text: admin：能进入安全页，看到密钥、主机、证书和配置包功能，但看不到“账号安全”。 root：还可以设置 root/admin 密码，或重置 admin 密码。这些密码管理接口会在后端校验root 身份。 Developer 设备：由设备证书的 OU 属性识别，不是登录账号。当前只有这类设备能导出配置包和 SSH 主机配置；以 root 登录不会改变设备身份。 除上述密码管理等自行校验身份的接口外，不能依靠“页面需要登录”阻止直接调用接口。网络隔离仍是当前使用前提。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 1.3 操作前的准备
entries.text: 确认地址栏 IP 对应目标设备，电脑也在可信管理网络中。 向服务器管理员确认 SSH 地址、端口和用户名。 使用页面部署或撤销公钥时，需要目标账户的密码，且该账户允许密码登录。不要为排障长期放宽服务器策略。 删除密钥、撤销授权或更换证书前，确认还有服务器控制台、另一管理员密钥或设备 HTTP 管理入口可用。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 修改设备登录密码
entries.text: 这里修改的是 TianShanOS 的登录密码，不是远端服务器的 SSH 密码。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 2.1 首次登录后的密码提醒
entries.text: 账号尚未标记为已修改密码时，登录后会出现改密提醒。请设置独有的长密码，不要选择“稍后修改”后长期保留默认密码。 这个提醒并不是随时可打开的账号设置入口。已经改过密码的 admin 用户如需再次改密，可由root 在安全页设置。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 2.2 由 root 设置密码
entries.text: 以 root 登录，打开“安全”。 在“账号安全”中点击“设置 root 密码”或“设置 admin 密码”。 两次输入相同的新密码并提交。界面接受 4-64 个字符；4 个字符只是技术下限，不是强度建议。 确认结果：用无痕窗口重新登录，确认新密码可用，再关闭原会话。修改密码不会自动结束已有会话。 登录失败时：先核对账号和设备 IP。连续 5 次失败会锁定约 5 分钟，不要反复猜测。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 2.3 重置 admin 密码
entries.text: root 可在账号安全区将 admin 重置为默认密码 rm01，并清除 admin 的登录锁定。重置后，立即用新会话登录 admin 并设置新密码。 重置是临时恢复手段。不要把默认密码留作日常使用，也不要把“修改密码”理解为已踢出所有旧会话。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 用 SSH 密钥连接服务器
entries.text: 首次设置按以下顺序进行：生成 RSA 密钥 → 部署公钥 → 测试连接 → 核对服务器身份。退役时，先撤销远端授权，确认不能再登录，最后删除本地密钥。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 3.1 生成密钥
entries.text: 在“密钥管理”中点击“生成新密钥”。 先查看已有列表，再输入未使用的密钥 ID，例如 backup01。不要复用旧 ID：当前生成接口没有重复 ID 拦截，可能覆盖原密钥。 选择 RSA 2048 或 RSA 4096。页面默认选 RSA 2048；虽然也列出 ECDSA，但当前 SSH 公钥认证不支持它。 按需填写备注和别名。只有确实需要备份或迁移私钥时，才勾选“允许导出私钥”；生成后没有修改此属性的页面入口。 点击“生成”，完成后刷新列表。 确认结果：找到正确的 ID 和 RSA 类型，点击“公钥”，确认完整文本以 ssh-rsa 开头。 注意：密钥列表容量为 8 个。满额时不要继续生成；先按撤销流程清理旧密钥。当前保存与列表登记并非完整的原子操作，成功提示后也要检查列表。“隐藏密钥 ID”不能保护真实 ID 不被接口读取。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 3.2 部署公钥
entries.text: 部署会将公钥追加到远端账户的 ~/.ssh/authorizedkeys，使设备有机会用对应私钥登录。它不会修改服务器密码。 在新密钥所在行点击“部署”。 填写服务器地址、用户名、SSH 端口和该账户的密码。 核对信息，点击“开始部署”。 完成后，在“已部署主机”检查对应记录，并按下一节测试。 当前流程先用密码完成 SSH 认证，再检查主机指纹；首次遇到的主机会被自动信任。它不能保证“确认服务器身份后才发送密码”。首次连接必须在受控网络中进行，事后比对指纹不能消除密码已经发出的风险。 提示成功但列表没有记录，或测试失败时：不要马上重复部署。远端公钥可能已经写入，只是密钥登录复验或本地保存失败。请从另一管理入口检查 authorizedkeys；反复部署可能追加重复行。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 3.3 测试连接并确认结果
entries.text: 在“已部署主机”核对地址、端口、用户名和密钥 ID。 点击“测试”。设备会尝试执行固定命令 echo "TianshanOS SSH Test OK"。 首次连接后，按第 4.3 节核对保存的主机指纹。 如何理解成功提示：页面只检查 API 请求是否成功，没有检查远端命令的退出码和回显内容。因此它是基础连接检查，不是完整验收，更不能证明 sudo 或业务命令可用。重要用途还需在实际任务中确认命令输出、退出码和权限。 测试失败时：先检查网络、SSH 服务、账户与远端授权。涉及指纹变化或服务器身份不明时，停止重试，按第 4.3 节处理。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 3.4 撤销远端授权，再删除本地密钥
entries.text: 确认另一条服务器管理入口可用，且设备上的原密钥尚未删除。 在“已部署主机”对应行点击“撤销”，输入服务器密码，确认“撤销并移除”。也可从密钥行发起撤销并填写目标信息。 查看撤销结果，再从可信的服务器管理入口检查 authorizedkeys，确认对应公钥及重复行已移除。 确认旧密钥不能再登录。撤销会留下 authorizedkeys.bak 备份；按服务器备份策略处理，避免以后恢复旧授权。 刷新本地主机列表。页面会尝试移除记录，但没有核对该移除请求的结果，必要时再手动“移除”。 所有目标服务器都处理完后，才删除设备中的旧密钥及不再需要的私钥副本。 提示“未找到公钥”：先从服务器侧确认选对账户且公钥确实不存在，再选择仅移除本地记录。 撤销失败或服务器身份可疑：保留本地密钥，改用可信控制台或另一管理员入口处理。不要继续向可疑服务器发送密码。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 管理密钥、主机与指纹

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 4.1 复制公钥和导出私钥
entries.text: 公钥：点击密钥行的“公钥”，复制完整的一行给服务器管理员。公钥不是秘密；发错对象本身不等于私钥泄露，也不要求立即换钥。管理员必须另行把它加入授权列表，才会产生访问权限。 私钥：只有生成时允许导出的密钥才能点击“私钥”导出。请在可信电脑和隔离网络中操作，保存到受控密钥库，并清理剪贴板、下载目录等临时副本。不要粘贴到聊天、工单或日志里。 复制按钮无响应：HTTP 页面可能无法使用浏览器剪贴板接口。可手动选中并复制可见文本，随后检查开头、结尾和内容是否完整。不要为方便复制而放宽浏览器安全设置。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 4.2 分清“撤销”“移除”和“删除”
entries.text: 操作 改变什么 撤销公钥 尝试删除服务器上的授权，需要远端密码 移除主机 删除设备本地的连接记录，不撤销服务器授权 删除密钥 删除设备本地密钥，不访问服务器，也不撤销授权 删除已知主机指纹 删除设备保存的服务器身份记录，不删除连接记录或服务器授权 “已部署主机”是本地清单，不会持续查询服务器。列表为空不代表远端授权已清理；列表中有记录也不代表现在仍能登录。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 4.3 核对 SSH 服务器指纹
entries.text: 指纹用于确认你连接的是哪台服务器。当前页面保存 SHA-256 摘要的 64 位十六进制值；常见OpenSSH 输出则是 SHA256:base64。先请管理员统一格式，不能直接比较这两种字符串。 首次连接后：在“已知主机指纹”点击“查看”，与服务器控制台、资产系统或另一条可信渠道提供的完整值比较。表格只显示前 32 位，不足以完成核对。 不一致时：停止连接并隔离调查。若已输入 SSH 密码，按可能泄露处理，通过可信入口修改密码、检查登录日志和清理不应存在的公钥。不要通过可疑连接执行页面撤销。 已保存的指纹发生变化时： 暂停重试，不要直接删除旧记录。 通过可信控制台核对新指纹、IP、端口、资产身份和维护记录。 只有确认是服务器重装或正常换钥后，才删除旧指纹。 在受控网络重新连接，再次查看并核对新记录。 页面当前可能只显示通用连接错误，不一定出现专门的指纹对比弹窗。 保管 SD 卡：指纹会保存到设备存储，并同步为 SD 卡明文 JSON。启动时有 SD 指纹配置就会以它为准替换对应 NVS 记录；文件没有签名保护。不要让不可信人员修改 SD 卡。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 4.4 导入和导出 SSH 主机配置
entries.text: 这是一条专用的 .tscfg 流程，与第 6 章尚未完成的通用配置应用不同。包中保存主机地址、端口、用户、认证类型和密钥 ID，不包含 SSH 密码或私钥，也不授予远端权限。 导出：在 Developer 设备上点击主机行“导出”，给另一设备使用时提供并核对目标设备证书，然后下载包。普通设备即使能看到按钮，后端也会拒绝导出。 导入： 确认包是为本设备制作的，SD 卡可写，并通过可信渠道核对来源。 确认本设备已有包所引用的正确密钥。只有相同 ID 不够，密钥本身也必须与服务器授权对应。 点击主机配置导入入口，选择文件并检查预览。只有确实要替换同名配置时才勾选覆盖。 确认后按提示重启。导入只把包保存到 SD 卡，重启时才尝试加载和解密。 检查加载后的地址、用户、端口和密钥 ID，再测试连接。 预览通过不等于可用：它既没有确认签名者可信，也没有核对接收设备指纹；目标检查要到重启加载时才执行。错误记录需要移除，并清理 SD 卡中对应包，避免重启后重新加载。更换设备证书前请同时阅读第 5.5 节。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 配置 HTTPS 证书与 mTLS
entries.text: 这部分面向证书管理员。当前 443 服务只提供健康、身份和权限测试接口，不提供完整管理页面。默认启动还需要设备私钥、设备证书和客户端 CA 链齐备。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 5.1 先分清证书方向
entries.text: 设备私钥和设备证书：让设备向连接它的客户端证明身份。 客户端证书和私钥：由电脑或服务持有，让客户端向设备证明身份。 安装在设备上的 CA 链：用于验证客户端证书，不会自动让电脑或浏览器信任设备证书。 双方都出示证书的方式叫 mTLS。客户端侧仍需配置信任设备证书的 CA，并校验访问名称和证书用途。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 5.2 生成设备私钥和证书申请
entries.text: 在“HTTPS 证书”点击“生成密钥对”。这会生成独立的 ECDSA P-256 私钥，与 SSH 密钥无关；本界面不能导出它。 已有私钥时先停止，按第 5.5 节确认替换影响；继续生成会覆盖旧私钥。 点击“生成 CSR”，填写设备 ID（CN）、组织（O）和组织单位（OU），或全部留空。 复制完整的 CSR 文本给 CA 管理员。CSR 是证书申请，不含私钥，也不会自动安装证书。 签发前必须检查名称：自定义字段路径不会生成 SAN；全部留空时，CN 固定为TIANSHAN-DEVICE-001，仅在能取得当前 IP 时加入该 IP 的 SAN，不含 DNS SAN。请让 CA 管理员核对 CSR，并通过受控签发流程把实际访问的 IP/DNS 加入最终证书 SAN；此表单不能编辑SAN。 确认结果：刷新后确认私钥存在；让 CA 管理员解析 CSR，核对公钥、主体和 SAN，并确认最终证书包含所需的服务器认证用途（EKU）。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 5.3 安装设备证书
entries.text: 取得与当前设备私钥匹配的 PEM 证书。 点击“安装证书”，粘贴包含首尾标记的完整文本并提交。 查看证书，核对主体、签发者和有效期。 成功提示只表示：证书可以解析，且公钥与当前私钥匹配。安装过程没有完整验证信任链、SAN、EKU、当前有效期或主体策略。 最终是否可信，要由实际客户端检查证书链、访问地址、用途和有效期。若提示密钥不匹配，先找回当前 CSR 对应的证书，不要为了消除错误而重新生成私钥。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 5.4 安装客户端 CA 链并测试
entries.text: 点击“安装 CA”，粘贴用于信任客户端证书的一个或多个 PEM CA 证书。 保留 HTTP 管理入口，安排重启设备后再测试。安装接口只更新存储，不会主动重启正在运行的443 服务。 使用受信任、用途及角色正确的客户端证书访问相应测试端点。 再使用不受信任的证书或不提供证书测试，确认连接被拒绝。 确认结果：设备使用预期的新证书；可信客户端只能访问其角色允许的接口，不可信客户端无法接入。具体握手和角色行为需要真机验收，不能仅凭安装提示确认。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 5.5 更新证书或删除全部凭证
entries.text: 仅证书到期：可以沿用未泄露的私钥申请新证书，安装后重新测试。但配置包绑定的是接收方证书指纹；即使沿用同一私钥，新证书指纹改变后，重新初始化或重启加载的旧包也会因目标不匹配而被拒绝。更换前请重新制作需要保留的包。 替换私钥：旧证书和旧 CSR 不再对应新私钥。这不等于旧证书已被 CA 吊销；若旧私钥泄露，应另行执行吊销和事件处理。没有旧私钥时，依赖它的旧包可能无法恢复。 删除全部 PKI 凭证：证书区的“删除凭证”会一起清除设备私钥、设备证书和客户端 CA 链。先确认 HTTP 管理入口可用，完成配置包替代安排，再确认删除。公开证书备份不能恢复私钥。 删除后刷新应显示未初始化；重启后检查 443 不再使用旧凭证。重新启用时需重新生成私钥、签发设备证书、安装 CA 链并完成测试。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 使用 Config Pack 前先看限制
entries.text: Config Pack 是加密、签名的 .tscfg 配置包。当前可以生成和检查包，但通用配置应用尚未完成，不要将它用于生产批量配置、灾难恢复或证明配置已经生效。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 6.1 各按钮目前实际做什么
entries.text: 操作 当前结果 导出设备证书 显示公开证书，供发送方为本设备制作包；不导出私钥 验证 检查包结构和自带证书对应的密文签名，不确认签名者可信或目标匹配 安全页选择/粘贴包后导入 前后端参数不匹配，当前不能完成导入 配置包列表中的导入 验证设备上已有文件，不复制、不解密、不应用 应用 解密并列出模块名，但没有写入模块配置；仍可能提示成功 Developer 导出配置包 生成可下载的加密签名包，并尝试保存到 SD 卡

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 6.2 核对来源，不要只看“签名有效”
entries.text: 接收设备目前用包内自带的证书检查签名，没有完成签名者证书链信任验证。签名保护的是包内密文，不应由此推断所有展示字段都已得到可信认证。“官方”字段也不能作为来源证明。 导入或检查前，通过资产系统或管理员认可的独立渠道核对签名者证书指纹、目标设备证书和包的用途。不要只凭同一封邮件同时收到的证书和指纹判断可信；预览里的目标名称也不能替代证书指纹核对。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 6.3 导出设备证书、检查收到的包
entries.text: 提供本设备证书：点击“导出设备证书”，复制完整 PEM 和显示的指纹，将公开证书交给发送方，再通过独立可信渠道核对指纹。 检查收到的包：打开“导入配置包”，选择或粘贴 .tscfg，点击“验证”。检查签名者信息并核对来源；验证不会应用配置，也不会证明包属于本设备。来源不明、目标不符或用途不清时停止。 即使验证通过，也不要继续依赖当前通用“导入”和“应用”完成配置。请回到对应功能页面使用已支持的设置方式，并检查实际结果。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 6.4 Developer 设备导出配置包
entries.text: 准备 SD 卡中的有效 JSON 配置文件，并取得已核对的目标设备证书。 点击“导出配置包”，选择文件，填写名称和说明，粘贴目标证书。 生成后下载 .tscfg。 分别检查浏览器下载文件和设备上的 /sdcard/outputconfig/ 保存结果。SD 保存失败时，接口仍可能返回包内容供下载。 导出不会修改源配置。发送给错误目标或接收方证书已更换时，需要重新生成包。当前接收端的通用应用功能仍未完成，不能因为导出成功就认为整个分发流程可用。

entries.title: 故障与安全事件处理

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 7.1 常见问题
entries.text: 现象 处理方式 看不到账号安全 用 root 登录；admin 不显示此区块 密钥生成成功但找不到 刷新列表并检查容量；不要复用 ID 或反复生成 ECDSA 部署失败 改用新 ID 生成 RSA 密钥；不要反复放宽服务器策略 部署成功但测试失败 从另一入口检查远端授权；不要直接重复部署 移除主机后仍能登录 移除仅清理本地记录，需另行撤销远端公钥 指纹变化或主机身份不明 停止连接，通过可信控制台核对，见第 4.3 节 安装证书后 443 不可用 检查私钥、设备证书、客户端 CA 链是否齐备，重启后用正确客户端证书测试 客户端仍报证书不可信 检查客户端信任库、SAN、EKU、有效期及证书链；设备内 CA 不是浏览器信任库 配置包应用成功但配置没变 当前实现没有写入模块配置，回到各功能页面操作

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 7.2 SSH 私钥可能泄露
entries.text: 限制设备和日志访问；当前日志可能包含私钥开头片段。 通过可信入口逐台撤销远端公钥，核对备份副本，确认旧密钥不能登录。 用新 ID 生成 RSA 密钥并重新部署，确认正常后删除旧密钥和导出副本。 检查相关登录日志。设备本地列表不一定覆盖所有曾授权的服务器。 如果泄露的是 HTTPS 私钥，按第 5.5 节替换设备凭证，并与 CA 管理员处理旧证书吊销及旧配置包。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 7.3 当前版本还需承担的风险
entries.text: 除前述 HTTP、接口鉴权、首次主机信任及配置包限制外，当前检查的构建配置未启用 NVS Encryption、Flash Encryption 和 Secure Boot。不能宣称设备私钥已得到这些存储和启动保护；实际设备的烧录配置与 eFuse 状态还需另行核验。 如使用场景无法接受这些限制，应暂停接入相应网络，由安全负责人决定隔离措施或产品修复。不要用操作手册中的验证步骤替代缺失的产品安全控制。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 8.1 本次如何核查
entries.text: 本指南对照了 d6ed947 基线下的当前工作区：页面操作和提示位于components/tswebui/web/js/app.js；API 行为位于 components/tsapi/src/；密钥与主机存储位于 components/tssecurity/src/；证书、443 服务及配置包分别位于components/tscert/、components/tshttps/ 和 components/tsconfigpack/。 重点复查了重复密钥 ID、测试退出码、撤销后的本地清理、证书指纹绑定，以及配置包未完成的导入/应用逻辑。这是静态代码核查；没有在本轮修改中连接远端服务器、变更设备凭证或进行真机安全验收。

entries.guideTitle: TianshanOS 安全页面完整操作指南
entries.title: 8.2 常用术语
entries.text: 公钥 / 私钥：公钥可交给授权方；私钥必须保密。服务器授权的是公钥，设备登录时使用对应私钥。 NVS：设备 Flash 中保存设置和密钥的存储区域；这个名称本身不表示数据已加密。 CSR / CA：CSR 是证书申请；CA 是签发或验证证书的机构或相应证书。 CN / O / OU：证书主体中的通用名、组织和组织单位。 SAN / EKU：分别说明证书可用于哪些访问名称或 IP，以及哪些认证用途。 PEM：带有 BEGIN/END 标记的文本格式，可用于证书、CSR 和密钥。 PKI / mTLS：PKI 是证书及信任管理体系；mTLS 是客户端和服务器双方都出示证书的连接方式。

entries.title: 1.1 Find the task you need
entries.text: Task Where to go Change the device's root or admin password Account Security; Chapter 2 Connect to a server using an SSH key Key Management and Deployed Hosts; Chapter 3 Copy keys or check a server's identity Key Management and host fingerprints; Chapter 4 Set up certificates and mutual authentication HTTPS Certificate; Chapter 5 Exchange encrypted configuration packages Config Pack; Chapter 6. General configuration application is not implemented yet

entries.title: 1.2 Accounts and device identity
entries.text: admin can open the Security page and see keys, hosts, certificates, and Config Pack controls, but not Account Security. root can also set the root and admin passwords or reset admin to its default password. These password-management operations enforce root authorization on the server. A Developer device is identified through the OU field in its device certificate. This is not a user account. Only these devices can currently export Config Packs and SSH host configurations; signing in as root does not change the device's identity. Except for operations such as password management that check authorization themselves, a login screen does not prevent direct API access. Network isolation remains a requirement.

entries.title: 1.3 Prepare for the operation
entries.text: Check that the IP address in your browser belongs to the intended device and that your computer is on a trusted management network. Confirm the SSH server address, port, and username with its administrator. To deploy or revoke a public key through this page, you need the remote account's password, and that account must accept password authentication. Do not leave server restrictions relaxed just to troubleshoot. Before deleting keys, revoking access, or replacing certificates, make sure you have another way in: a server console, a separate administrator key, or the device's HTTP management interface.

entries.title: Change device passwords
entries.text: These controls change TianShanOS login passwords, not the SSH password on a remote server.

entries.title: 2.1 The password prompt after sign-in
entries.text: If an account is still marked as having an unchanged password, a password-change prompt appears after sign-in. Set a long, unique password. Choosing to change it later dismisses the prompt; it does not make the default password safe to keep. This prompt is not an account-settings screen that you can reopen at any time. If admin has already changed its password and needs another change, root can set it from the Security page.

entries.title: 2.2 Set a password as root
entries.text: Sign in as root and open Security. Under Account Security, select Set root password or Set admin password. Enter the same new password twice and submit. The interface accepts 4-64 characters; four characters is a technical minimum, not a security recommendation. Check the result: sign in with the new password in a private browsing window before closing your original session. Changing a password does not automatically end existing sessions. If sign-in fails: check the account and device address first. Five consecutive failed attempts trigger a lockout of about five minutes. Avoid repeated guesses.

entries.title: 2.3 Reset the admin password
entries.text: root can reset admin to the default password, rm01, and clear its login lockout. After resetting, sign in as admin in a new session and set a new password immediately. A reset is a temporary recovery measure. Do not keep the default password, and do not assume a password change signs out every existing session.

entries.title: Connect to a server with an SSH key
entries.text: For initial setup: create an RSA key, deploy its public key, test the connection, then check the server fingerprint. When retiring a key, revoke access on the servers first, confirm that the old key no longer works, and only then delete the local key.

entries.title: 3.1 Create a key
entries.text: In Key Management, select Generate New Key. Check the existing list and choose an unused key ID, such as backup01. Do not reuse an ID: the generation API does not reject duplicates and may overwrite the existing key. Choose RSA 2048 or RSA 4096. RSA 2048 is the interface default. ECDSA options are shown, but the current SSH public-key authentication path does not support them. Add a comment or alias if useful. Allow private-key export only if you need it for backup or migration; there is no interface for changing this setting later. Select Generate, wait for completion, and refresh the list. Check the result: find the intended ID and RSA type. Open Public Key and check that the complete text starts with ssh-rsa. Keep in mind: the key list holds eight entries. Do not keep generating keys when it is full; retire an unused key first. Key storage and list registration can succeed or fail separately, so check the list even after a success message. Hide Key ID does not prevent the API from exposing the real ID.

entries.title: 3.2 Deploy the public key
entries.text: Deployment appends the public key to the remote account's ~/.ssh/authorizedkeys, allowing that account to accept the matching private key. It does not change the server password. Select Deploy on the new key's row. Enter the server address, username, SSH port, and that account's password. Review the details and select Start Deploy. Check for the server under Deployed Hosts, then test it as described below. The current implementation authenticates with the password before checking the host fingerprint, and automatically trusts previously unknown hosts. It does not guarantee that the server's identity is verified before the password is sent. Make the first connection on a controlled network; checking the fingerprint afterward cannot undo password exposure. If deployment reports success but the record is missing or the test fails: do not immediately deploy again. The public key may already be installed even though the follow-up key test or local record save failed. Check authorizedkeys through another management connection. Repeated deployment can append duplicate entries.

entries.title: 3.3 Test the connection
entries.text: Under Deployed Hosts, check the address, port, username, and key ID. Select Test. The device attempts to run echo "TianshanOS SSH Test OK". After the first connection, check the saved host fingerprint using Section 4.3. What success means: the page checks whether the API operation succeeded, but does not check the remote command's exit status or output. Treat this as a basic connection check, not a complete acceptance test. It does not establish that sudo or your application commands will work. For an important workload, verify the actual command's output, exit status, and permissions. If the test fails: check connectivity, the SSH service, the account, and remote authorization. Stop retrying if the fingerprint has changed or the server's identity is uncertain; follow Section 4.3.

entries.title: 3.4 Revoke access before deleting the local key
entries.text: Confirm that another server-management connection works and that the original key still exists on the device. Select Revoke on the host row, enter the server password, and confirm Revoke & Remove. You can also start from the key row and enter the target details. Review the result, then use a trusted server-management connection to check that the public key and any duplicate entries are gone from authorizedkeys. Confirm that the old key can no longer sign in. Revocation leaves an authorizedkeys.bak backup; handle it under the server's backup policy so an old authorization is not restored later. Refresh the local host list. The page attempts to remove the record but does not check that request's result. Remove the record manually if it remains. Only after every target server is handled should you delete the old key from the device and remove unneeded private-key copies. If no matching public key is found: confirm on the server that you selected the correct account and that the key is absent before choosing to remove only the local record. If revocation fails or the server looks suspicious: keep the local key and use a trusted console or another administrator connection. Do not keep sending a password to a server whose identity is in doubt.

entries.title: 4.1 Copy a public key or export a private key
entries.text: Public key: select Public Key and copy the complete, single-line value for the server administrator. A public key is not secret. Sending it to the wrong person does not by itself expose the private key or require key replacement. Access is granted only when an administrator adds it to an account's authorization list. Private key: export is available only if you enabled it when the key was created. Use a trusted computer on an isolated network, store the key in an approved secret store, and clear temporary copies from the clipboard and download folder. Never paste it into chat, tickets, or logs. If Copy does nothing: browsers may block clipboard access on an HTTP page. Select and copy the visible text manually, then check that the beginning, end, and full contents are intact. Do not weaken browser security settings just to enable copying.

entries.title: 4.2 Revoke, Remove, and Delete are different
entries.text: Action Effect Revoke a public key Attempts to remove authorization on the server; requires the remote password Remove a host Deletes the device's local connection record, not remote authorization Delete a key Deletes local key material; does not contact the server or revoke access Delete a host fingerprint Deletes a saved server-identity record, not the connection record or remote authorization Deployed Hosts is a local list, not a live view of server authorization. An empty list does not prove that remote access has been removed, and a listed host is not guaranteed to be reachable.

entries.title: 4.3 Check the SSH server fingerprint
entries.text: A fingerprint identifies the server you are connecting to. This page stores the SHA-256 digest as 64 hexadecimal characters. OpenSSH tools commonly show SHA256:base64 instead. Ask the administrator to provide the same format before comparing; the strings are not directly interchangeable. After the first connection: open the full fingerprint with View in the host-fingerprint section. Compare it with a value obtained from a server console, asset inventory, or another trusted channel. The table shows only the first 32 characters, which is not enough for the full check. If they differ: stop connecting and investigate in isolation. If you entered an SSH password, treat it as potentially exposed. Use a trusted connection to change it, review sign-in logs, and remove any unwanted public-key authorization. Do not use the suspicious connection to revoke access through this page. If a previously saved fingerprint changes: Stop retrying. Do not simply delete the old entry. Use a trusted console to verify the new fingerprint, IP address, port, asset identity, and maintenance record. Delete the old fingerprint only after confirming an authorized server rebuild or host-key change. Reconnect on a controlled network, then view and check the new saved fingerprint. The current page may show a generic connection error rather than a dedicated fingerprint-comparison dialog. Protect the SD card: fingerprints are stored locally and synchronized to plaintext JSON on the card. At startup, available SD fingerprint configurations replace the corresponding NVS records. These files are not signed; do not allow untrusted changes to them.

entries.title: 4.4 Import and export SSH host configurations
entries.text: This dedicated .tscfg workflow is separate from the unfinished general configuration application in Chapter 6. A host package contains the address, port, username, authentication type, and key ID. It contains neither the SSH password nor the private key, and it does not grant access on the server. To export: on a Developer device, select Export on the host row. Supply and verify the target device's certificate when exporting for another device, then download the package. An ordinary device may show the button, but the backend rejects its export request. To import: Confirm that the package was made for this device, the SD card is writable, and the source has been verified through a trusted channel. Make sure this device already has the correct key referenced by the package. A matching ID alone is not enough; the key material must match the server's authorization. Select Import Host, choose the file, and review the preview. Enable overwrite only when you intend to replace an existing configuration with the same name. Confirm and restart as prompted. Import saves the package to the SD card; loading and decryption are attempted at restart. Check the loaded address, username, port, and key ID, then test the connection. A successful preview is not proof that the package will work. It neither establishes trust in the signer nor checks the recipient fingerprint. The target check happens during loading after restart. Remove an incorrect record and its corresponding SD package to prevent it from loading again. Before replacing the device certificate, also read Section 5.5.

entries.title: Configure HTTPS certificates and mTLS
entries.text: This chapter is for certificate administrators. The current service on port 443 offers only health, identity, and permission-test endpoints, not the full web interface. With its default settings, startup requires a device private key, a device certificate, and a client CA chain.

entries.title: 5.1 Know which certificate does what
entries.text: The device certificate and private key let the device prove its identity to a connecting client. A client certificate and private key, held by a computer or service, let that client prove its identity to the device. The CA chain installed on the device is used to verify client certificates. It does not automatically make a computer or browser trust the device certificate. This two-way certificate exchange is called mutual TLS, or mTLS. The client must still trust the CA that issued the device certificate and check its name and permitted uses.

entries.title: 5.2 Generate a device key and certificate request
entries.text: Under HTTPS Certificate, select Generate Key Pair. This creates a separate ECDSA P-256 private key, unrelated to SSH keys. It cannot be exported through this interface. If a key already exists, stop and review Section 5.5 before proceeding. Generating another key overwrites the old one. Select Generate CSR. Enter the device ID (CN), organization (O), and organizational unit (OU), or leave all fields blank. Send the complete CSR text to your CA administrator. A CSR requests a certificate; it contains no private key and does not install a certificate. Check names before issuance: the custom-field path does not generate a SAN. With all fields blank, the CN is fixed at TIANSHAN-DEVICE-001; the current IP is included as an IP SAN only if it can be obtained. No DNS SAN is added. Have your CA administrator inspect the CSR and use a controlled issuance process to put the required IP addresses or DNS names in the final certificate's SAN. This form cannot edit SANs. Check the result: refresh the page to confirm that the private key exists. Have the CA administrator inspect the CSR's public key, subject, and SAN, and ensure that the issued certificate has the required server-authentication purpose (EKU).

entries.title: 5.3 Install the device certificate
entries.text: Obtain a PEM certificate that matches the device's current private key. Select Install Cert, paste the full text including its boundary markers, and submit. View the certificate and check its subject, issuer, and validity dates. The success message means only that the certificate can be parsed and its public key matches the current private key. Installation does not fully validate the trust chain, SAN, EKU, current validity, or subject policy. The actual client must check the chain, access name, purposes, and validity. If installation reports a key mismatch, locate the certificate issued for the current CSR. Do not generate a new private key simply to clear the error.

entries.title: 5.4 Install the client CA chain and test
entries.text: Select Install CA and paste one or more PEM CA certificates used to trust your clients. Keep the HTTP management interface available and schedule a device restart before testing. Installation updates storage but does not actively restart the running service on port 443. Access the relevant test endpoints using a trusted client certificate with the correct purpose and role. Repeat with an untrusted certificate or no certificate, and confirm that the connection is rejected. Check the result: the device presents the intended new certificate; trusted clients can access only the endpoints allowed for their roles, and untrusted clients cannot connect. Handshake and role behavior must be tested on the device, not inferred from an installation message.

entries.title: 5.5 Renew certificates or delete all credentials
entries.text: For certificate expiry alone: you can reuse an uncompromised private key to request a new certificate, install it, and test again. However, Config Packs are tied to the recipient certificate's fingerprint. Even with the same private key, a changed certificate fingerprint causes old packages to be rejected as belonging to another recipient after reinitialization or restart. Arrange replacement packages before changing the certificate. When replacing the private key: the old CSR and certificate no longer match the new key. This does not revoke the old certificate at the CA. If the old key was exposed, handle revocation and incident response separately. Packages that depend on a lost private key may be unrecoverable. To delete all PKI credentials: Delete Credentials in the certificate section clears the device private key, device certificate, and client CA chain together. Verify your HTTP recovery access and arrange replacement packages before confirming. A backup of the public certificate cannot restore a private key. After deletion, refresh the page and check for an uninitialized state. Restart and verify that port 443 no longer uses the old credentials. To restore the service, generate a new key, obtain and install a device certificate, install the CA chain, and repeat the tests.

entries.title: Understand Config Pack limitations
entries.text: A Config Pack is an encrypted, signed .tscfg package. The current implementation can create and inspect packages, but general configuration application is unfinished. Do not rely on it for production fleet configuration, disaster recovery, or proof that settings have changed.

entries.title: 6.1 What the controls currently do
entries.text: Action Current result Export Device Certificate Shows the public certificate so a sender can create a package for this device; does not export the private key Verify Checks structure and the ciphertext signature against the included certificate; does not establish signer trust or recipient identity Import after selecting or pasting a package Frontend and backend parameters do not match; this flow cannot complete Import from the package list Validates an existing device file; does not copy, decrypt, or apply it Apply Decrypts and lists module names without writing module settings; may still report success Export Config Pack on a Developer device Creates a downloadable encrypted, signed package and attempts to save it to the SD card

entries.title: 6.2 Verify the source, not just the signature
entries.text: The recipient currently checks the signature using the certificate included in the package. Signer certificate-chain trust validation is not implemented. The signature covers the ciphertext; do not assume that every displayed metadata field is therefore authenticated. An Official label is not proof of a trusted source either. Before importing or inspecting a package, use an asset system or an independent, approved channel to confirm the signer certificate fingerprint, target certificate, and intended change. Receiving a certificate and its fingerprint together in one email is not an independent check. The target name shown in the preview is not a substitute for checking the certificate fingerprint.

entries.title: 6.3 Share the device certificate and inspect a package
entries.text: To provide this device's certificate: select Export Device Certificate, copy the full PEM and displayed fingerprint, and send the public certificate to the sender. Confirm the fingerprint through a separate trusted channel. To inspect a received package: open Import Config Pack, select or paste the .tscfg file, and select Verify. Review the signer details and check the source. Verification does not apply settings or prove that this device is the recipient. Stop if the source, target, or purpose is unclear. Even if verification passes, do not rely on the current general Import and Apply controls to configure the device. Use the supported controls on the relevant feature pages and check the actual settings afterward.

entries.title: 6.4 Export a package from a Developer device
entries.text: Prepare valid JSON configuration files on the SD card and obtain a verified target-device certificate. Select Export Config Pack, choose the files, enter a name and description, and paste the target certificate. Generate and download the .tscfg file. Check the browser download and the saved file under /sdcard/outputconfig/ separately. If the SD write fails, the API may still return the package for download. Export does not modify the source settings. Regenerate a package made for the wrong target or an obsolete recipient certificate. Successful export does not establish that the full distribution workflow works: general application on the receiving device is still unfinished.

entries.title: 7.1 Common problems
entries.text: Symptom What to do Account Security is missing Sign in as root; admin does not see this section Key creation reports success, but the key is missing Refresh the list and check capacity; do not reuse IDs or repeatedly generate keys ECDSA deployment fails Create an RSA key with a new ID; do not repeatedly relax server policy Deployment succeeds, but Test fails Check remote authorization through another connection before deploying again Access still works after removing a host Remove affects only the local record; revoke the remote public key separately A fingerprint changes or the server's identity is unclear Stop connecting and verify through a trusted console; see Section 4.3 Port 443 fails after certificate installation Check the device key, certificate, and client CA chain; restart and test with a suitable client certificate A client still rejects the certificate Check the client trust store, SAN, EKU, validity, and chain; the device's CA store is not the browser's trust store Apply succeeds, but settings do not change Module settings are not written by the current implementation; use the relevant feature pages

entries.title: 7.2 Suspected SSH private-key exposure
entries.text: Restrict device and log access. Current logs may contain the beginning of a private key. Revoke the public key on every affected server through trusted connections. Check backup copies and confirm that the old key no longer works. Create and deploy a new RSA key under a new ID. Once it works, delete the old key and exported copies. Review sign-in logs. The device's local list may not include every server where the key was authorized. If the HTTPS private key was exposed instead, replace the device credentials as described in Section 5.5 and work with the CA administrator on certificate revocation and old packages.

entries.title: 7.3 Other current security risks
entries.text: In addition to the HTTP, authorization, first-connection trust, and package limitations already described, the inspected build configuration does not enable NVS Encryption, Flash Encryption, or Secure Boot. Do not claim that these mechanisms protect stored private keys or startup integrity. The firmware actually flashed to a device and its eFuse settings require separate checks. If your use case cannot tolerate these limitations, keep the device out of that network or trust environment until the security owner approves isolation measures or a product fix. Checks in a user guide cannot replace missing product security controls.

entries.title: 8.1 Basis of this guide
entries.text: The review used the current working copy based on d6ed947. Page behavior and messages are in components/tswebui/web/js/app.js; API behavior is in components/tsapi/src/; key and host storage are in components/tssecurity/src/. Certificates, the port 443 service, and packages are implemented in components/tscert/, components/tshttps/, and components/tsconfigpack/. Specific checks covered duplicate key IDs, SSH test exit-status handling, local cleanup after revocation, recipient certificate fingerprints, and unfinished package import and application logic. This was a static review: this revision did not connect to remote servers, change device credentials, or perform security acceptance tests on hardware.

entries.title: 8.2 Terms used in this guide
entries.text: Public key / private key: share the public key with an administrator who grants access; keep the private key secret. Authentication uses the matching pair. NVS: a Flash storage area for device settings and keys. The name does not imply encryption. CSR / CA: a certificate signing request, and a certificate authority or its certificate. CN / O / OU: common name, organization, and organizational unit fields in a certificate subject. SAN / EKU: the names or IP addresses a certificate covers, and the authentication purposes it permits. PEM: a text format with BEGIN/END markers, used for certificates, CSRs, and keys. PKI / mTLS: the certificate and trust-management system, and mutual TLS, in which both the client and server present certificates.

entries.title: 先了解两条网络连接路径
entries.text: RM-01 提供两条基于 USB-C 的网络连接路径，本文分别称为 C1 接口和 C3 接口。两者都能承载网络连接，但连接对象和网络拓扑不同： 接口 主要用途 连接后的网络关系 C1 将电脑、平板或手机等用户设备接入 RM-01 用户设备加入 RM-01 内部交换机网络，成为内部网络中的一个节点 C3 将 RM-01 接入用户现有的局域网 通过 LPMU 为其他内部节点提供路由，使整机接入交换机或路由器所在的上层网络

entries.title: C1 接口
entries.text: C1 位于机身侧后方。面对上下排列的两个 USB-C 接口时，C1 是靠上的接口；接口下方刻有连接图样，可用于确认位置。

entries.title: C3 接口
entries.text: C3 位于机身顶部。掀开上方磁吸盖板后，可以看到该 USB-C 接口。C3 是顶部共享 USB 接口，可在 TianshanOS 中切换至 ESP、AGX 或 LPMU。

entries.title: 通过 C1 将用户设备接入 RM-01
entries.text: 使用支持数据传输的 USB-C 线缆，将 iPad、电脑、手机或其他用户设备连接至 C1。连接后，RM-01 会自动完成 DHCP 地址分配，用户无需手动填写 IP 地址、网关或 DNS。 用户设备通常会识别出一个名为 AX88179 或 USB Ethernet 的有线网络接口。该设备随后会加入 RM-01 内部交换机网络，并可以与内部网络中的设备通信。 C1 会把用户设备直接接入 RM-01 内部网络。只连接可信设备；在公共或不受信任环境中，不要把未经管理的设备接入 C1。

entries.title: 保留互联网连接并向 RM-01 共享网络
用户设备的互联网连接可能发生什么
entries.text: 连接 C1 后，部分操作系统可能把 AX88179 当作优先网络出口。由于 C1 首先用于访问 RM-01 内部网络，而不是直接提供互联网，用户设备原有的互联网连接可能暂时中断。 如果用户设备仍需通过 Wi-Fi、以太网或其他连接访问互联网，应确保原有互联网连接的优先级高于 AX88179： 系统 系统中的名称 设置原则 macOS 网络服务顺序（Service Order） 将提供互联网的 Wi-Fi 或以太网置于 AX88179 之上 Windows 接口跃点数（Interface Metric） 数值越小优先级越高；使互联网接口的跃点数小于 AX88179 Linux 路由 metric（Route Metric） 数值越小优先级越高；使互联网默认路由的 metric 小于 AX88179

entries.title: 使用 RM-01 网络连接工具
entries.text: 如果还需要把用户设备的互联网连接共享给 RM-01，请从网站的“下载”页面获取 RM-01 网络连接工具。该工具会配置用户设备与 C1 之间的 DHCP、路由和网络共享规则，使互联网流量能够从用户设备转发至 RM-01 内部网络。 当前支持： macOS Linux Windows 专业版 Windows 家庭版当前不受支持。 网络连接工具会修改用户设备的网络地址、路由和共享设置，运行时可能短暂中断现有连接。开始前请保存正在进行的下载、远程会话和其他依赖网络的工作。

entries.title: 使用 AI 配置 C1 网络共享
entries.text: 具备本机命令执行能力的 Agent Harness（如 Codex、Hermes）可以根据自然语言检查网络拓扑，并帮助配置从用户电脑到 RM-01 内部网络的转发与共享。这里的 AI 必须能够在目标电脑上执行系统命令；普通对话式 AI 只能提供操作建议，不能直接完成配置。

entries.title: 在哪里运行 AI Agent
entries.text: 建议直接在连接 C1 的用户电脑上运行 Agent。因为互联网出口、默认路由和共享规则都由这台电脑管理，Agent 需要获得该电脑的管理员权限才能完成配置。 如果 Codex、Hermes 或其他 Agent 运行在 RM-01 内部，则必须事先获得对用户电脑的远程命令执行权限和管理员授权；否则它无法修改用户电脑上的网络共享、路由与防火墙设置。

entries.title: 执行前确认
entries.text: 用户电脑已经通过 C1 接入 RM-01，并能看到名为 AX88179 或 USB Ethernet 的网络接口。 用户电脑的 C1 地址为 10.10.99.100/24，RM-01 内部节点仍使用 10.10.99.99、10.10.99.98 和 10.10.99.97。 用户电脑已经通过 Wi-Fi、以太网或其他接口正常访问互联网。 Agent Harness 可以在用户电脑上执行命令，并可在需要时请求管理员权限。 已保存下载、远程会话及其他依赖网络的工作，并能够在本机恢复网络配置。

entries.title: 可直接发送给 Agent 的提示词
entries.text: 下面的提示词保留了 RM-01 的出厂网络拓扑，同时要求 Agent 先检查、再修改，并给出验证与回滚方法。可以直接复制到 Codex、Hermes 或其他具备命令执行能力的 Agent Harness： 你正在帮助我为 RM-01 配置 C1 网络共享。请先检查当前系统、网络接口、地址、默认路由和防火墙状态，确认实际情况与下述拓扑一致后再执行修改；不要仅凭接口名称猜测，也不要改动 RM-01 内部节点的固定地址。 当前拓扑如下： 用户电脑通过 USB-C 连接 RM-01 的 C1 接口；该连接在用户电脑上通常显示为 AX88179 或 USB Ethernet，地址为 10.10.99.100/24。 RM-01 内部网络为 10.10.99.0/24。 应用计算机（LPMU）地址为 10.10.99.99。 推理计算机（AGX）地址为 10.10.99.98。 带外管理计算机地址为 10.10.99.97。 用户电脑还通过另一个网络接口连接互联网。 我的目标是：保留用户电脑现有的互联网连接，并把该连接通过 C1 对应的 AX88179 / USB Ethernet 接口共享给 RM-01 内部网络，使 10.10.99.99、10.10.99.98 和 10.10.99.97 能够访问互联网。 请按以下约束操作： 先识别操作系统、实际互联网出口接口和 C1 对应接口，并向我说明准备修改的项目。 使用当前操作系统原生且改动最小的网络共享方式，配置必要的 IP 转发、NAT、路由或 Internet Connection Sharing。 不要改变用户电脑现有互联网接口的优先级和默认路由，不要改动上述 RM-01 节点地址，也不要清空或覆盖无关的防火墙规则。 如需管理员权限，请明确说明用途后再请求；如果当前系统或权限无法安全完成配置，请停止并说明原因。 完成后验证：用户电脑仍可访问互联网；10.10.99.99、10.10.99.98、10.10.99.97 可达；RM-01 内部节点可以访问公网 IP，并能正常解析域名。 最后列出实际执行的命令或修改项、验证结果，以及恢复原配置的回滚步骤。 macOS 通常使用“互联网共享”及系统路由机制；Linux 通常使用 IP 转发与 nftables 或 iptables；Windows 专业版通常使用 Internet Connection Sharing（ICS）。具体命令和接口名称应以 Agent 在当前电脑上的检查结果为准。Windows 家庭版当前不受支持。

entries.title: 如何判断配置成功
entries.text: 配置完成后，应同时满足以下条件： 用户电脑原有的互联网连接保持可用。 用户电脑可以访问 10.10.99.99、10.10.99.98 和 10.10.99.97。 RM-01 内部节点既能访问公网 IP，也能解析并访问域名。 Agent 已给出实际修改项和可执行的回滚步骤，而不是只报告“配置成功”。

entries.title: 安全提示
entries.text: 允许 Agent 以管理员或 root 权限配置网络，会使其能够修改路由、IP 转发、NAT、Internet Connection Sharing 和防火墙规则。只使用可信的 Agent Harness，并在授权前核对其操作计划。若用户电脑正承担远程连接或其他关键网络任务，请先确保可以在本机恢复配置。

entries.title: 通过 C3 将 RM-01 接入上层网络
entries.text: 这里的“上层网络”是指用户已有的局域网，例如交换机或路由器所在的网络。

entries.title: 准备连接器
entries.text: 用户需自备以下连接设备： 一个 USB-C ↔ RJ45 以太网适配器 一根连接交换机或路由器的 RJ45 网线 将 USB-C 端连接至 C3，再将 RJ45 网线连接至用户的交换机或路由器。仅完成物理连接还不足以完成 DHCP 和路由配置，后续必须运行 RM-01 内置的网络配置程序。

entries.title: 将顶部 USB 切换至 LPMU
entries.text: 打开 TianshanOS 首页。 找到“USB 切换”区域。 点击“USB”按钮，将顶部 USB 接口的当前目标切换至 LPMU。 确认页面显示的当前目标为 LPMU 后，再继续网络配置。 切换顶部 USB 目标时，当前连接可能短暂断开。请勿在接口正在传输数据时切换目标。

entries.title: 通过 LPMU 完成整机联网
entries.text: RM-01 出厂时已在 LPMU 中预制网络自动化配置项目。LPMU 取得上层网络连接后，会通过内部路由与 NAT 为 AGX 等内部节点转发流量，使整机接入用户的上层网络。

entries.title: 项目位置和用户需要做什么
entries.text: 项目位于 LPMU 当前用户的主目录，预制路径为 ~/network-setup/，其中面向 LPMU 的脚本位于 ~/network-setup/lpmu/。 出厂设备不需要重新下载项目，也不需要重复执行 README 中面向工程部署的 scp、chmod 或安装步骤。普通用户应从 TianshanOS 运行配置；只有在故障诊断或二次开发时，才需要进入项目目录检查脚本与日志。 请勿随意移动、重命名或删除 ~/network-setup/。TianshanOS 的网络配置功能依赖出厂预制的项目路径和脚本。

entries.title: 自动化项目会完成什么
entries.text: 执行配置后，项目会在 LPMU 上依次完成以下工作： 检测具有网关的网络接口，并通过连通性测试选择可用的上层网络出口。 重新设置 LPMU 的默认路由，使流量通过选定的上层网络接口发送。 启用 IPv4 转发，并配置 iptables 的 NAT 与 FORWARD 规则。 使内部 AGX（默认地址 10.10.99.98）通过 LPMU（内部地址 10.10.99.99）访问上层网络。 配置用于访问 AGX 的端口转发规则。 项目还包含可选的智能路由监控服务。启用后，服务每 30 秒检查一次当前网络出口，在连接失效时尝试切换至其他可用接口，并在首选接口恢复后切换回来。

entries.title: 通过 TianshanOS 运行
entries.text: 确认 C3 已通过 USB-C ↔ RJ45 以太网适配器连接至交换机或路由器。 确认 TianshanOS 首页中的顶部 USB 目标已经切换至 LPMU。 在 TianshanOS 顶部导航中打开“网络”。 找到“接入上层网络”。 点击“通过LPMU接入”。 等待状态从“处理中”变为“成功”或“失败”。处理期间不要重复启动。 状态显示“成功”表示脚本已找到可用的上层网络出口、完成 LPMU 路由配置，并执行内部网络转发与 NAT 配置。此时仍建议验证 AGX 的 IP 连通性和 DNS 解析，而不是仅以按钮状态作为最终判断。

entries.title: 如何确认联网成功
entries.text: 首先确认 TianshanOS 显示“成功”。如果用户拥有 AGX 终端权限，可在 AGX 中依次执行： ping -c 3 10.10.99.99 # 验证 AGX 到 LPMU ping -c 3 8.8.8.8 # 验证互联网 IP 连通性 ping -c 3 google.com # 验证 DNS 解析 三项测试分别验证内部链路、互联网转发和 DNS。第一项失败通常表示内部连接或地址配置异常；第一项成功而第二项失败，应检查 LPMU 的上层网络、默认路由和 NAT；前两项成功而第三项失败，则应检查 DNS 配置。

entries.title: 端口转发与安全边界
entries.text: 当前项目会在 LPMU 的上层网络接口配置以下转发： LPMU 入口 转发目标 用途 TCP 58022 AGX TCP 22 通过 LPMU 访问 AGX 的 SSH 服务 TCP/UDP 58000–58999 AGX 相同端口 访问运行在 AGX 上的应用服务 例如，SSH 客户端连接的是 LPMU 的上层网络地址，但用户名和认证凭据属于 AGX： ssh -p 58022 <AGXUSERNAME>@<LPMUIP> 端口转发会扩大 AGX 服务在上层网络中的可访问范围。只应在可信局域网中启用，并结合交换机、路由器或上层防火墙限制来源地址；不要把这些端口直接暴露到公共互联网。

entries.title: 风险与故障排查
entries.text: “通过LPMU接入”会删除 LPMU 的旧默认路由，清空现有 iptables NAT 表和 FORWARD 链规则，并把 FORWARD 默认策略设置为 DROP，随后再写入 RM-01 所需的路由、NAT 与端口转发规则。该过程可能立即中断远程连接，也会覆盖已有的自定义网络和防火墙配置。若 LPMU 做过定制，请先导出路由表与防火墙规则，并确保具备本地恢复方式。 如果接入失败，请依次检查： C3 使用的 USB-C ↔ RJ45 适配器和网线是否连接牢固。 交换机或路由器端口是否已经启用。 TianshanOS 首页显示的顶部 USB 目标是否为 LPMU。 上层网络是否能向 LPMU 提供有效地址、网关和 DNS。 “接入上层网络”区域显示的错误和输出信息。 AGX 是否仍可访问 LPMU 内部地址 10.10.99.99。 LPMU 中是否存在与默认路由、NAT、FORWARD 链或端口转发冲突的自定义规则。

entries.title: Understand the Two Network Paths
entries.text: RM-01 provides two USB-C-based network paths, referred to in this guide as the C1 port and the C3 port. Both carry network connections, but they connect different devices and create different network topologies: Port Primary purpose Network relationship after connection C1 Connect a computer, tablet, phone, or other user device to RM-01 The user device joins the RM-01 internal switch network as an internal network node C3 Connect RM-01 to the user's existing local network LPMU routes traffic for the other internal nodes, allowing the complete system to join the upstream switch or router network

entries.title: C1 port
entries.text: C1 is on the rear side of the enclosure. Of the two vertically arranged USB-C ports, C1 is the upper port. A connection symbol engraved below the port helps identify it.

entries.title: C3 port
entries.text: C3 is on top of the enclosure. Lift the magnetic top cover to expose this USB-C port. C3 is the shared top USB port and can be switched among ESP, AGX, and LPMU in TianshanOS.

entries.title: Connect a User Device through C1
entries.text: Use a USB-C cable that supports data transfer to connect an iPad, computer, phone, or other user device to C1. RM-01 automatically provides DHCP configuration, so the user does not need to enter an IP address, gateway, or DNS server manually. The user device will normally detect a wired network interface named AX88179 or USB Ethernet. The device then joins the RM-01 internal switch network and can communicate with devices on that network. C1 connects the user device directly to the RM-01 internal network. Connect only trusted devices, and do not attach unmanaged devices to C1 in public or untrusted environments.

entries.title: Keep Internet Access and Share It with RM-01
What may happen to the user device's internet connection
entries.text: After C1 is connected, some operating systems may treat AX88179 as the preferred network path. Because C1 provides access to the RM-01 internal network rather than direct internet access, the user device's existing internet connection may be interrupted. If the user device must continue using Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or another connection for internet access, keep that internet connection at a higher priority than AX88179: System System terminology Configuration principle macOS Network service order (Service Order) Place the internet-providing Wi-Fi or Ethernet service above AX88179 Windows Interface metric Lower values have higher priority; use a lower metric for the internet interface than for AX88179 Linux Route metric Lower values have higher priority; use a lower metric for the internet default route than for AX88179

entries.title: Use the RM-01 Network Connection Tool
entries.text: To share the user device's internet connection with RM-01, obtain the RM-01 Network Connection Tool from the website's Downloads page. The tool configures DHCP, routing, and network-sharing rules between the user device and C1 so internet traffic can be forwarded into the RM-01 internal network. Currently supported systems: macOS Linux Windows Pro Windows Home is not currently supported. The network connection tool changes network addressing, routing, and sharing settings on the user device. Existing connections may be interrupted briefly. Save active downloads, remote sessions, and other network-dependent work before starting.

entries.title: Configure C1 Internet Sharing with AI
entries.text: An Agent Harness with local command-execution capability, such as Codex or Hermes, can inspect the network topology from natural-language instructions and help configure forwarding and internet sharing from the user computer to the RM-01 internal network. The AI must be able to execute system commands on the target computer. A chat-only AI can provide instructions but cannot apply the configuration.

entries.title: Where to run the AI agent
entries.text: Run the agent directly on the user computer connected to C1 whenever possible. That computer owns the internet uplink, default route, and sharing rules, so the agent needs administrator access on that computer to perform the configuration. If Codex, Hermes, or another agent runs inside RM-01, it must already have authorized remote command execution and administrator access to the user computer. Without that access, it cannot change network sharing, routing, or firewall settings on the user computer.

entries.title: Confirm before starting
entries.text: The user computer is connected to RM-01 through C1 and can see a network interface named AX88179 or USB Ethernet. The C1 address on the user computer is 10.10.99.100/24, while the RM-01 internal nodes remain at 10.10.99.99, 10.10.99.98, and 10.10.99.97. The user computer already has working internet access through Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or another interface. The Agent Harness can execute commands on the user computer and request administrator privileges when required. Active downloads, remote sessions, and other network-dependent work have been saved, and the network can be recovered locally if needed.

entries.title: Prompt to send directly to the agent
entries.text: The following prompt preserves the factory RM-01 topology, requires inspection before modification, and asks for validation and rollback instructions. Copy it into Codex, Hermes, or another command-capable Agent Harness: You are helping me configure C1 internet sharing for RM-01. First inspect the current operating system, network interfaces, addresses, default routes, and firewall state. Make changes only after confirming that the actual configuration matches the topology below. Do not infer interface roles from names alone, and do not change the fixed addresses of the RM-01 internal nodes. Current topology: The user computer is connected by USB-C to the C1 port on RM-01. On the user computer, this connection normally appears as AX88179 or USB Ethernet and uses 10.10.99.100/24. The RM-01 internal network is 10.10.99.0/24. The application computer (LPMU) is 10.10.99.99. The inference computer (AGX) is 10.10.99.98. The out-of-band management computer is 10.10.99.97. The user computer also has internet access through a separate network interface. My goal is to preserve the user computer's existing internet connection and share it through the AX88179 / USB Ethernet interface associated with C1, allowing 10.10.99.99, 10.10.99.98, and 10.10.99.97 to access the internet. Follow these constraints: Identify the operating system, the actual internet uplink, and the interface associated with C1, then explain what you plan to change. Use the operating system's native, least-invasive sharing method to configure only the necessary IP forwarding, NAT, routing, or Internet Connection Sharing. Do not change the priority or default route of the user computer's existing internet interface. Do not change the RM-01 node addresses above, and do not flush or overwrite unrelated firewall rules. If administrator privileges are required, explain why before requesting them. If the current system or permissions cannot complete the configuration safely, stop and report the reason. After applying the configuration, verify that the user computer still has internet access; 10.10.99.99, 10.10.99.98, and 10.10.99.97 are reachable; and the RM-01 internal nodes can reach a public IP address and resolve DNS names. Finally, list the commands or settings actually changed, the validation results, and the rollback steps required to restore the original configuration. macOS normally uses Internet Sharing and system routing facilities; Linux typically uses IP forwarding with nftables or iptables; and Windows Pro normally uses Internet Connection Sharing (ICS). Exact commands and interface names must follow the agent's inspection of the current computer. Windows Home is not currently supported.

entries.title: How to confirm that it worked
entries.text: All of the following conditions should be true after configuration: The user computer's original internet connection remains available. The user computer can reach 10.10.99.99, 10.10.99.98, and 10.10.99.97. RM-01 internal nodes can reach both public IP addresses and internet hostnames through DNS. The agent reports the exact changes made and provides executable rollback steps instead of only stating that the configuration succeeded.

entries.title: Security notice
entries.text: Granting an agent administrator or root access for network configuration allows it to change routes, IP forwarding, NAT, Internet Connection Sharing, and firewall rules. Use only a trusted Agent Harness and review its proposed actions before authorizing them. If the user computer carries a remote session or other critical network workload, make sure the configuration can be recovered locally first.

entries.title: Connect RM-01 to an Upstream Network through C3
entries.text: In this guide, “upstream network” means the user's existing local network, such as a network provided by a switch or router.

entries.title: Prepare the adapter
entries.text: The user must provide: A USB-C-to-RJ45 Ethernet adapter An RJ45 Ethernet cable connected to the switch or router Connect the USB-C end to C3, then connect the RJ45 cable to the user's switch or router. The physical connection alone does not complete DHCP or routing configuration. The built-in RM-01 network configuration program must be run afterward.

entries.title: Switch the top USB port to LPMU
entries.text: Open the TianshanOS home page. Find “USB Switch.” Select the “USB” button and switch the current target of the top USB port to LPMU. Confirm that the page shows LPMU as the current target before continuing. Switching the top USB target may disconnect the current link briefly. Do not switch targets while data is being transferred through the port.

entries.title: Bring the Complete System Online through LPMU
entries.text: RM-01 ships with the network automation project preloaded on LPMU. After LPMU obtains upstream connectivity, it uses internal routing and NAT to forward traffic for AGX and the other internal nodes, bringing the complete system onto the user's upstream network.

entries.title: Project location and what the user needs to do
entries.text: The project is stored in the home directory of the current LPMU user at ~/network-setup/. LPMU-specific scripts are located in ~/network-setup/lpmu/. On a factory-configured device, do not download the project again or repeat the engineering deployment steps in the repository README, such as scp, chmod, or service installation. Regular users should start the configuration from TianshanOS. Enter the project directory only for troubleshooting or development. Do not move, rename, or delete ~/network-setup/. The TianshanOS network configuration workflow depends on the factory project path and scripts.

entries.title: What the automation project configures
entries.text: When started, the project performs the following work on LPMU: Detects interfaces with gateways and runs connectivity tests to select a usable upstream path. Replaces the LPMU default route so traffic uses the selected upstream interface. Enables IPv4 forwarding and configures iptables NAT and FORWARD rules. Allows the internal AGX, at the default address 10.10.99.98, to reach the upstream network through LPMU at 10.10.99.99. Adds port-forwarding rules for services hosted on AGX. The project also includes an optional smart-route monitoring service. When enabled, it checks the current upstream path every 30 seconds, attempts to fail over when connectivity is lost, and returns to the preferred interface when that interface recovers.

entries.title: Run the configuration from TianshanOS
entries.text: Confirm that C3 is connected to the switch or router through the USB-C-to-RJ45 Ethernet adapter. Confirm that the top USB target on the TianshanOS home page is set to LPMU. Open “Network” from the top navigation in TianshanOS. Find “Upstream Network Access.” Select “Access via LPMU.” Wait for the state to change from “Processing” to “Success” or “Failed.” Do not start the operation again while it is processing. “Success” means that the script found a usable upstream path, configured the LPMU route, and ran the internal forwarding and NAT configuration. Verify AGX IP connectivity and DNS resolution afterward instead of treating the button state as the only proof of connectivity.

entries.title: Confirm that the connection works
entries.text: First confirm that TianshanOS reports “Success.” If the user has AGX terminal access, run these checks on AGX: ping -c 3 10.10.99.99 # Verify AGX-to-LPMU connectivity ping -c 3 8.8.8.8 # Verify internet IP connectivity ping -c 3 google.com # Verify DNS resolution These checks isolate the internal link, internet forwarding, and DNS. If the first test fails, inspect the internal link and addressing. If the first succeeds but the second fails, inspect the LPMU upstream connection, default route, and NAT. If only the third fails, inspect DNS configuration.

entries.title: Port forwarding and the security boundary
entries.text: The current project configures these forwards on the LPMU upstream interface: LPMU entry Forwarding target Purpose TCP 58022 AGX TCP 22 Reach the AGX SSH service through LPMU TCP/UDP 58000–58999 The same ports on AGX Reach application services running on AGX For SSH, the client connects to the LPMU upstream address, but the username and authentication credentials belong to AGX: ssh -p 58022 <AGXUSERNAME>@<LPMUIP> Port forwarding increases the reachability of AGX services from the upstream network. Enable it only on a trusted LAN and restrict source addresses with the switch, router, or upstream firewall. Do not expose these ports directly to the public internet.

entries.title: Risks and troubleshooting
entries.text: “Access via LPMU” deletes the previous LPMU default routes, flushes the existing iptables NAT table and FORWARD chain, sets the default FORWARD policy to DROP, and then writes the RM-01 routing, NAT, and port-forwarding rules. This can immediately interrupt remote sessions and overwrite custom network or firewall configuration. If LPMU has been customized, export the current routes and firewall rules first and make sure a local recovery path is available. If the operation fails, check the following in order: Confirm that the USB-C-to-RJ45 adapter and Ethernet cable connected to C3 are secure. Confirm that the switch or router port is enabled. Confirm that the TianshanOS home page shows LPMU as the current top USB target. Confirm that the upstream network provides LPMU with a valid address, gateway, and DNS configuration. Read the error and output shown in “Upstream Network Access.” Confirm that AGX can still reach the LPMU internal address 10.10.99.99. Check for custom LPMU rules that conflict with the default route, NAT, FORWARD chain, or port forwarding.
